0.long_answer: Disulfide bonds in proteins are critical for maintaining proper protein structure, and they are formed by the oxidation of the sulfhydryl groups in cysteine residues. Although cysteine is the amino acid that directly forms these bonds, it is considered conditionally essential because the body can synthesize it from methionine when sufficient methionine is available. Methionine is an essential amino acid; this means it must be provided in the diet because the body cannot synthesize it. A deficiency in methionine will limit the body’s ability to produce cysteine, thereby impairing the formation of disulfide bonds in proteins. Thus, a methionine deficiency impairs the body’s capacity to synthesize the necessary cysteine.
